sampling_model.design: One consecutive trajectory in the fixed common path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) from a stationary regime \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\); identification is population-level and sampling uncertainty comes from temporal dependence.
sampling_model.units: Overlapping finite cylinders \(C_{\mathcal A}(S,a)\) on the fixed product alphabet, indexed by their terminal time.
sampling_model.treatment: A hypothetical intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x)\); no experimental assignments are observed.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cylinder assignment in the fixed product alphabet has positive probability, hence every denominator cylinder used by the returned expression is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Probabilities of the returned \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders are estimated by empirical frequencies and their long-run covariance by the modified-Bartlett Newey--West estimator with \(h_T\to\infty\) and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives sufficient summary-graph front-door conditions and a common do-free expression for selected micro total effects under latent confounding.
The ID algorithm returns an observational functional or a hedge and is complete for a fixed finite ADMG.
Theorem 1.1 bounds the graph segment needed to decide identification for one fully specified periodic latent-confounded time-series graph.
A possible-c-component and region recursion is sound and complete for causal identification over the finite graph class represented by a PAG.
Fixing kernels and intrinsic sets characterize identifiable effects and nested constraints in a fixed ADMG.
Do-calculus is sound and complete for macro total effects in latent-confounded summary causal graphs.
A complete graphical characterization and two finite adjustment sets identify linear direct effects from summary causal graphs under no hidden confounding.
Under causal sufficiency, Theorem 2 gives sufficient summary-graph conditions and a finite adjustment set for singleton lag-specific total effects.
Necessary and sufficient conditions and a pseudo-linear algorithm characterize identification by common adjustment in causally sufficient summary graphs.
Graphical fixing outputs can be compiled into weight-based and influence-function estimators under independent sampling.

body.tldr: The full sound-and-complete lag-robust fixing theorem remains open, but the terminating three-way certified procedure now has two imported graph-native success regions in addition to its existing concrete and saturated-ID rules. After the Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui causally sufficient adjustment test, it deterministically checks every nonempty macro-mediator set against Assaad's 2025 four-condition latent-confounded SCG front-door criterion, only for \(\gamma\in\{0,L\}\), and returns the source's explicit nested finite-cylinder functional for the first passing set. The local proof establishes the required full-time-ADMG class inclusion and positivity of every denominator; no necessity or generic-family inclusion is claimed. The verified binary lag-switch pair remains the direct failure certificate, all other undecided inputs return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\), and the conservative transition bound is \(6+2^{n-2}+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}\). Every success supports the existing cylinder plug-in and HAC delta-method inference under the stated positivity, mixing, bandwidth, and variance conditions.

project_justification.gap: Published SCG adjustment covers a substantial causally sufficient region, and Assaad (2025), Theorem 1 covers a selected latent-confounded front-door region, but neither gives a sound-and-complete decision rule for lag-specific micro effects over the present fixed-alphabet stationary refinement class. Fixed-graph hedges likewise do not automatically preserve time homogeneity, exact summary, positivity, equality of the entire observed process law, and unchanged coordinate alphabets under a refinement switch.
project_justification.niche: The attainable contribution is certified partial identification with graph-native abstention. The procedure faithfully imports both the published causally sufficient adjustment region and the published latent-confounded SCG front-door region, adds saturated-ID successes for acyclic loop-free directed summaries, and gives a direct cyclic lag-switch nonidentification pair. Precisely the two displayed lag-switch refinements each admit their own refinement-specific identifying functional; no assertion is made that every refinement in the full class is individually identifiable. Remaining latent-confounded cyclic cases require the still-open offset-sensitive normal form and direct fixed-alphabet witness construction.
project_justification.fill: The ordered procedure recognizes one proved outside-front-door success, one proved positive stationary lag-switch failure, the explicit 2024 adjustment branch, and then, for \(\gamma\in\{0,L\}\), at most \(2^{n-2}-1\) nonempty mediator sets under Assaad's 2025 SCG front-door criterion. A first passing set returns the displayed two-stage cylinder functional; otherwise the procedure uses a memoized ordinary-ID call on at most \(n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}\) ancestral roles when the directed summary is acyclic and loop-free. All remaining cases return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\), preserving the honest absence of a completeness claim.

body.related_work: Assaad (2025), Theorem 1 supplies the four-condition SCG front-door criterion for selected micro-query lags under latent confounding and its common two-stage do-free formula. The present procedure imports that result explicitly: it enumerates macro-mediator sets, constructs the source's mediator block and two temporal adjustment blocks, and proves that every local bounded-lag stationary semi-Markovian SCM induces a candidate full-time ADMG in the source class. Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui (2024) separately give sufficient graphical conditions and finite adjustment sets under causal sufficiency; that criterion remains the preceding branch. Ferreira and Assaad treat macro effects and linear direct effects, while Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier characterize common adjustment under causal sufficiency. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman bound identification for one specified periodic fine graph; Jaber and coauthors decide a finite graph class represented by one PAG; Shpitser and Pearl prove ID soundness and completeness for one finite ADMG; and Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser develop fixed-ADMG fixing and intrinsic sets. These imported results do not supply the offset-sensitive cross-refinement normal form or fixed-alphabet rejection construction required for completeness. The note's local claims are therefore the typed stationary transfers, the certified ordered combination, and the explicit lag-switch obstruction, not novelty of either published sufficient criterion.
body.interpretation: A success tag is a positive causal certificate. It may arise from the concrete outside-front-door rule, the imported causally sufficient adjustment rule, the imported Assaad latent-confounded SCG front-door rule, or a successful saturated ordinary-ID call; in every case the returned finite-cylinder arithmetic functional equals the lag-specific intervention probability in every compatible SCM. A failure tag remains a negative certificate consisting of two fixed-alphabet stationary SCMs with the same entire observational process law and different targets. An unknown tag is neither. EasyRCA ranks only successful queries and reports the provenance of the functional; it displays failures and unresolved cases separately rather than converting either into a low transmission score.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The two imported SCG branches are only sufficient. The adjustment branch excludes bidirected summaries, while the Assaad front-door branch is restricted to \(\gamma\in\{0,L\}\), a passing macro-mediator set, and its stated cycle condition. In the remaining region, a finite rejection witness may contain several temporal roles of the same observed coordinate; independent-shift replication then attempts to place several role values into one coordinate-time variable, while product-slot repairs enlarge the fixed alphabet. The procedure therefore constructs only its displayed failure pair directly and returns unknown elsewhere. Strict stationarity and bounded structural lag do not make the observed process finite-order Markov, so transition-kernel truncation and semantic gluing of refinement-specific formulas still cannot establish completeness.
body.honest_scope: The note proves sound partial certification, not a sound-and-complete TID-SCG dichotomy. Both published branches are imported coverage: the 2024 rule applies under causal sufficiency and its stated sufficient graphical condition, while the 2025 rule applies only in its stated query-lag regime and when a nonempty macro-mediator set passes all four SCG front-door conditions. No necessity, novelty, or equality with the note's unproved generic front-door family is claimed for either criterion. The acyclic saturated-ID branch is sound but not complete for uniform identification, the concrete outside-family witness remains separate, and the direct failure branch covers only the verified binary lag-switch query. Latent-confounded cyclic cases outside these rules remain open. The two displayed lag-switch refinements each have a refinement-specific identifying functional, but that fact is not generalized to every refinement. The HAC theorem applies only after a sound success and additionally requires cylinder positivity, geometric beta mixing, the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).
